Scientists Introduce Synthetic Material That Efficiently Pulls CO2 From the Air
What's the catch? Is it expensive? Energy-cost prohibitive to produce? There must be one or this would be bigger news, wouldn't it?

It's not big news because so far it's only a material that catches and releases CO2 in wet or dry air. A machine would have to be made to cycle a sheet of this stuff and remove the CO2. At that point you still have the CO2 in the machine, and something needs to be done with it. Stripping off the oxygen is another step that could be materially, energetically, economically, or environmentally expensive. And then you have to ask how many of these machines you need to really make a difference. If they can be sold as consumer commodities ("Just run this machine and you're carbon neutral! Run two and you can use your minivan guilt free!") AND if they catch on, AND if people are willing to pay the maintenance and energy cost then they could indeed make the human race carbon neutral. If they would have to be built, deployed, and maintained by governments that's much less likely to happen. And so far such a machine hasn't been built. Just the material. And we don't even know if the material can be mass produced or at what cost. Another use exists: as a possible more efficient CO2 scrubber for industry, but again so far this isn't a machine that can do that.

tl;dr: It's just some stuff in a laboratory for now.

No, air moves about much too quickly and easily for an imbalance to occur. Theoretically if such a machine exists there's the slight possibility of a houseplant or two dying because a sealed house or apartment with no one at home and the CO2 scrubbed starved them. Aside from the various costs of operating the machines that's pretty much the limit of negative effects.

Hey everyone... I'm nokster, a long time gamer (CS, TFC, TF2, UT, AoE, bla bla bla) and electronic music enthusiast :)

I work for a large software company and we recently had an internal "Innovation Contest" to come up with new ideas. Successful projects have come from these types of internal brainstorming sessions, but almost always these have been enterprise and business oriented. Which got me and some of my co-workers thinking, why not try a different approach? As gamers, we all had a problem with the current crop of voice chat solutions. The established apps have become aged and bloated. Many of the newcomers never really delivered on what they promised.

The result of this thinking was wRekt: our new, browser based voice chat for gamers that runs on our existing infrastructure.

TL;DR:

New, browser based voice chat for gamers.
We think we're different because we could potentially be backed by the company we work for, if we demonstrate to our execs that there is enough interest.
We've built a basic alpha version and need your feedback to grow and add features.

Our site: https://wrekt.me/

How to stay updated:
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/WrektMe
Twitter: https://twitter.com/wrektme
Mailing list: Here

Also, we're running a gaming headset giveaway until the end of April, if you need additional incentive!

How it works:

  1. Log in to wRekt using social sign in (we plan to add e-mail sign up, we only collect your name and e-mail though).
  2. Create a new room.
  3. Send the generated link to your friends to invite them into the room.
  4. Chat!

Why we're different:

  • No downloading - browser based
  • No server required - we host everything
  • Completely free
  • Fast - You're logged in and chatting in moments
  • wRekt is not WebRTC based like many of the recent attempts at new browser-based voice chat have been. There is fully dedicated infrastructure mixing the audio, and sending/receiving the streams.
  • Our infrastructure can support many concurrent users with no user impact.

What do we need / how can you help?:

  • We need to grow our current user base. We work on this project in our free time and have gotten it this far, but we do not yet have the proper resources to take this thing to the next level. We have upcoming meetings with our execs where, if we can prove that there is enough interest, our request for additional resources will hopefully be granted.
  • We need your feedback!! We want to know what features are the most demanded among voice chat users. There are the obvious features that we would like to add next, but the more data we can gather, the better. There is a dedicated form within wRekt ("Tell us how we're doing" link) or you can reply here.

What's in it for you?

  • We intend to provide some sort of perks for our most dedicated early users if and when our project takes off. This is obviously a long way out, but we have discussed possibilities and fully intend to reward our early supporters somehow, when we are able to.
  • You try it first! You will be the first to test new features and see changes as they happen.
  • You get to support a group of dedicated gamers like yourselves! The entire group working on this project is made up of gamers. We play LoL, CS, CoC, TF2, and Far Cry 4, among other games.

Business Plan

As with anything else, there needs to be some sort of revenue to make wRekt sustainable. Our plan is to offer the basic voice chat service for free, with some additional features available for a small premium. At this early stage, we don’t yet know what those premium features will be and how much they will cost, but we intend to keep the pricing fair.

What else should you know?

As mentioned earlier... this is a basic version of what we ultimately hope to achieve. You may encounter bugs. You may find certain features lacking. With your help and input, though, we will hopefully be able to evolve into something great!

So that's it. Thank you all in advance!!
